correctness.rationale: Verified analytically and by re-running verify_coloring.py (all checks pass). Interior opposite-octant classes are independent since same-pattern dots are strictly positive and opposite-pattern strictly negative. Boundary admissibility criterion (sign-cancellation in sum s_i z_i |y_i|) is correct, lists {1,2}/{3,4}, {1,3}/{2,4}, {1,4}/{2,3} derived correctly and respected by assignment. Lemma enumerating Z-neighbours (same-circle +-90-degree mates plus opposite-circle poles) checked by direct dot computations; mates always flip sign-quadrant so colours 1-vs-4/4-vs-2 differ; axes vs opposite circles and inter-axis colours differ; all coincident colours occur only on proven non-edges. Partition interior/axes/arcs is exhaustive. Proof is analytic; script is supporting evidence only.

originality.rationale: FAIL: headline chi<=4 (hence not chi>=5) for radius-1/sqrt2 orthogonality graph is substantively implied by the known stronger exact value chi=4 for the unit-sphere orthogonality graph (Godsil-Zaks arXiv:1201.0486 Lemma 1.1, whose note states the result was already known before 1988). Radial scaling x->sqrt(2)x is a graph isomorphism preserving orthogonality, so unit-sphere chi=4 implies submitted chi<=4. Detailed recolouring is therefore a recomputation/certificate/repackaging of a known stronger fact, not a new claim. ADMISSION_DEFECT: admission missed this direct prior coverage of the target question.

value.rationale: In isolation the result type is independently valuable: an explicit proper 4-colouring negatively resolving the motivated TARGET question chi>=5 for a natural sphere orthogonality graph, with exact object and invariant fixed before computation, non-trivial case analysis, and honest limitation to {3,4} via the triangle lower bound. It is not a type/normalization error, vacuity, cheap small-instance mismatch, direct lookup, or arbitrary-parameter fact. Priority failure is recorded under originality, not re-litigated here.
